title: Security Ask Orchestration Lifecycle and Priority Lattice
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers submit a wide variety of non-bug security and compliance asks (SOC2 evidence requests, vendor questionnaires, DPA clarifications, HIPAA scoping, GDPR data residency questions). Today intake is ad-hoc across email, Zendesk, and sales threads. That creates inconsistent SLAs, duplicated work between PM/Ops/Security, and long lead times for customers.

Goal: Design and deliver an orchestration lifecycle and a priority lattice that standardizes routing, automated triage, and a lightweight QA gate for responses. The solution should: 1) categorize requests into deterministic buckets, 2) attach a priority and SLA, 3) route to the right responder(s) (Docs/Security/Support/Legal), and 4) provide a QA/approval step for high-risk responses before outbound communication.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New intake form + webhook captures structured metadata for 90% of incoming requests (type, vendor, sensitivity, deadline).
2) Priority lattice maps every request type into P0/P1/P2/P3 with clear SLA rules implemented in triage runbook.
3) Automated routing reduces manual handoffs by 60% in pilot accounts.
4) QA gate triggers for requests marked high-risk and tracks approval timestamps in ticket metadata.
5) Playbook and templated responses published in Confluence with owner assignments.
success_metrics:
- Mean time to first response for security asks <= 48 hours for P1 and <= 7 days for P2/P3.
- Manual handoffs per ticket reduced by 60% in Q2 pilot.
- >80% of questionnaire answers reused from canonical library.
- NPS/CSAT for enterprise compliance interactions improved by 0.25 points in pilot cohort.

decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Decision: Use a deterministic priority lattice rather than ML classification for first phase to keep behavior auditable. Rationale: simplicity and compliance requirements.
- Tradeoff: The lattice will be conservative (more requests flagged as higher priority) to avoid missed escalations; this increases QA workload initially but reduces risk.
- Decision: Reuse existing Zendesk + lightweight webhook layer for routing instead of building a new intake portal. Rationale: fastest path to production for pilot.
- Tradeoff: UX is less polished than a custom portal; plan to iterate on a dedicated intake UI in Q3 if pilot metrics justify it.
open_risks:
- Risk: High volume of vendor questionnaires could still overwhelm the canonical answer library; need content triage and a content owner.
- Risk: Slack-based QA approvals may not meet enterprise audit requirements; mitigation: persist approvals in audit log (Confluence/GCS) and loop Legal for high-risk items.
- Risk: Dependencies on ENG-4420 (routing infra) could delay automation. Contingency: manual routing runbook for interim.

playbook_snippets:
If request type == 'SOC2 evidence' AND deadline <= 7 days => Priority P0; route to Security + Solutions Eng.
If vendor_questionnaire score > 0.6 (automated heuristic) => attach questionnaire template + assign to Solutions Eng.
QA gate rules: Any request tagged 'high-risk' or 'legal-review' requires at least one Security and one Legal approver before closing. Approval timestamp must be recorded in ticket metadata.
